catalyst_text: Presented encouraging Phase 1 responses in NSCLC
detailed_catalyst_text: Preliminary Phase 1 monotherapy data in previously treated NSCLC showed a 56.0% confirmed ORR and 88.0% DCR in CEAhigh patients, with many responses ongoing at cutoff. Grade 3 or higher TEAEs were mainly hematologic, including anemia and neutropenia. The program also received FDA Fast Track designation in 2026-10.
catalyst_text_evidence: As of 2026-04-09, preliminary Phase 1 monotherapy findings from 43 heavily pretreated patients with NSCLC, including 25 with high CEA expression, showed: Confirmed ORR was 56.0% in patients with CEAhigh NSCLC, with a disease control rate of 88.0%; confirmed ORR in the overall NSCLC population was 34.9%. Among patients with CEAhigh NSCLC, median duration of response had not been reached. The majority of responders, as well as two patients with unconfirmed responses, remained on treatment at data cutoff. Grade 3 or higher treatment-emergent adverse events (TEAEs) were predominantly hematologic events (anemia 14.0%, neutropenia 14.0%, thrombocytopenia 2.3%). BG-C477 received Fast Track Designation from the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) in 2026-10.

catalyst_text: Reported positive Phase 1 results in hepatocellular carcinoma
detailed_catalyst_text: Updated Phase 1 data in heavily pretreated hepatocellular carcinoma showed a 36% confirmed ORR at the selected Phase 3 dose with low rates of high-grade treatment-related events. The program has received FDA Fast Track (2025-12) and Orphan Drug designations in the US (2026-03) and EU (2026-10). These results highlight meaningful activity and a favorable safety profile in a late-line population.
catalyst_text_evidence: Updated Phase 1 results include the first disclosure of dose-optimization data and longer follow-up from dose escalation. At the recommended Phase 3 dose of 450 mg every three weeks, the confirmed objective response rate (ORR) was 36.0%, a result that exceeds efficacy observed with TKIs, which have shown an ORR of approximately 5% in late-line HCC. Across dose levels, Grade 3 or higher treatment-related adverse events occurred in 5.3% of patients, and treatment-related adverse events led to discontinuation in only 2.1%. BGB-B2033 received Fast Track Designation from the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) in 2025-12, as well as Orphan Drug Designation from the FDA in 2026-03 and the European Commission in 2026-10 for hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC).

catalyst_text: Global Phase 3 trial now enrolling patients
detailed_catalyst_text: A global Phase 3 trial (KANDELA-302) in first-line HR+/HER2-negative advanced or metastatic breast cancer is enrolling to compare the agent plus letrozole against standard CDK4/6 inhibitors plus letrozole. Enrollment began in 2026-05 across multiple regions. This reflects advancement into a pivotal setting for this selective CDK4 inhibitor.
catalyst_text_evidence: Building on previously reported Phase 1 activity and tolerability findings, BeOne is advancing BGB-43395, an investigational selective CDK4 inhibitor, in the global Phase 3 KANDELA-302 study (NCT07492641). Enrollment began in 2026-05, with patients planned across North and South America, Europe, Asia and Australia. The study compares BGB-43395 plus letrozole with investigator’s choice of abemaciclib, palbociclib or ribociclib plus letrozole in first-line HR+/HER2-negative advanced or metastatic breast cancer.

catalyst_text: Reported promising Phase 1 activity in NSCLC
detailed_catalyst_text: Initial Phase 1 findings in MTAP-deficient NSCLC showed a confirmed ORR of 25.3% (38.5% in EGFR wild-type) with median PFS of 7.7 months overall and 8.1 months in EGFR wild-type. Intracranial responses were observed in untreated, asymptomatic brain metastases with a 30.8% intracranial ORR, and safety was manageable at 200–400 mg daily. These data indicate systemic and CNS activity in a biomarker-selected population.
catalyst_text_evidence: BGB-58067 is a highly potent, brain-penetrant methylthioadenosine (MTA)-cooperative PRMT5 inhibitor designed to exploit the vulnerability created by MTAP deficiency. In this, the largest publicly shared data set in MTAP-deficient solid tumors, initial Phase 1 findings from 182 patients, including 83 with NSCLC, showed: Among 75 efficacy-evaluable patients with MTAP-deficient NSCLC, confirmed ORR was 25.3% and disease control rate (DCR) was 76.0%. In the EGFR wild-type subgroup, confirmed ORR was 38.5% and DCR was 82.1%. Median progression-free survival was 7.7 months in the overall NSCLC cohort and 8.1 months in the EGFR wild-type subgroup. In the NSCLC cohort, an intracranial objective response rate of 30.8% was observed in patients with untreated, asymptomatic brain metastases as well as a low rate of central nervous system (CNS) progression in 2L+ NSCLC. At daily doses of 200–400 mg (n=87), Grade 3 or higher treatment-related adverse events occurred in 27.6%, and treatment-related adverse events led to discontinuation in 5.7%.

catalyst_text: Announced positive survival results from Phase 3 study
detailed_catalyst_text: Reported updated Phase 3 HERIZON-GEA-01 results in first-line HER2-positive gastroesophageal adenocarcinoma. The triplet with chemotherapy achieved median OS of 27.0 months versus trastuzumab plus chemotherapy (HR 0.65) and 36-month OS of 39.8%; adding the PD-1 to zanidatamab plus chemotherapy showed a four-month OS improvement but was not statistically significant versus the doublet.
catalyst_text_evidence: BeOne Medicines Ltd. ... announced new survival results from the planned second interim analysis (IA2) and final formal analysis of the Phase 3 HERIZON-GEA-01 trial, further confirming the benefit of TEVIMBRA ... plus ZIIHERA ... and chemotherapy as first-line treatment for patients with HER2-positive locally advanced or metastatic gastroesophageal adenocarcinoma (GEA). TEVIMBRA plus ZIIHERA and chemotherapy demonstrated sustained long-term survival versus trastuzumab plus chemotherapy. Median OS was 27.0 months, with an OS hazard ratio (HR) of 0.65 (95% CI: 0.52-0.80), improved from 0.72 at the first interim analysis. Long-term survival was highest with the TEVIMBRA-containing regimen. Estimated 36-month OS was 39.8% with TEVIMBRA plus ZIIHERA and chemotherapy, 31.5% with ZIIHERA plus chemotherapy and 22.9% with trastuzumab plus chemotherapy. Adding TEVIMBRA to ZIIHERA plus chemotherapy was associated with a four-month longer median OS at 27.0 months compared with ZIIHERA plus chemotherapy with 22.9 months (HR 0.81; 95% CI: 0.65-1.00).

catalyst_text: Trial met primary endpoint with significant survival benefit
detailed_catalyst_text: Phase 3 HERIZON-GEA-01 showed the doublet of zanidatamab plus chemotherapy significantly improved overall survival versus trastuzumab plus chemotherapy in first-line HER2-positive gastroesophageal adenocarcinoma. Median OS was 22.9 months versus 19.6 months (HR 0.76; P=0.0088), meeting the remaining primary endpoint.
catalyst_text_evidence: ZIIHERA plus chemotherapy significantly improved OS versus trastuzumab plus chemotherapy. Median OS was 22.9 months versus 19.6 months, respectively (HR 0.76; 95% CI: 0.62-0.93; P=0.0088), meeting the remaining primary endpoint of the study.

detailed_catalyst_text: The company announced positive topline results from the second interim analysis of the Phase 3 HERIZON-GEA-01 trial of zanidatamab plus chemotherapy, with or without tislelizumab, in first-line HER2-positive locally advanced or metastatic gastroesophageal adenocarcinoma. These Phase 3 topline data represent a key milestone suggesting clinical benefit for first-line HER2-positive GEA.

drug_indication: HER2-Positive Gastric or Gastroesophageal Junction Cancer
catalyst_text: Received FDA approval for HER2 positive gastric cancer
detailed_catalyst_text: The FDA approved a supplemental Biologics License Application for the PD-1 inhibitor in combination with zanidatamab and chemotherapy for first-line treatment of adults with unresectable locally advanced or metastatic HER2-positive gastric or gastroesophageal junction cancer. This approval enables use of the combination regimen in the United States and expands treatment options for HER2-positive gastric/GEJ disease.

(Nasdaq: ONC; HKEX: 06160; SSE: 688235), a global oncology company, today announced that the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has approved the supplemental Biologics License Application (sBLA) for TEVIMBRA® (tislelizumab) in combination with ZIIHERA® (zanidatamab) and chemotherapy for the first-line treatment of adult patients with unresectable locally advanced or metastatic HER2-positive (HER2+) gastric, gastroesophageal junction.

catalyst_text: Announced positive Phase 3 topline results meeting primary endpoint
detailed_catalyst_text: The Phase 3 MANGROVE trial in previously untreated mantle cell lymphoma reported positive topline results, meeting the primary endpoint of progression-free survival. The regimen of the BTK inhibitor plus rituximab showed a 43% reduction in risk of progression or death with safety consistent with known profiles, supporting a chemotherapy-free frontline approach that could impact standard of care.
catalyst_text_evidence: BeOne Medicines Ltd. ... today announced positive topline results from the Phase 3 MANGROVE study ... in adult patients with previously untreated mantle cell lymphoma (MCL). For this prespecified interim analysis, MANGROVE met its primary endpoint of progression-free survival (PFS), demonstrating a highly statistically significant and clinically meaningful improvement for BRUKINSA plus rituximab versus BR, as assessed by an independent review committee (IRC). This BRUKINSA-based, chemotherapy-free regimen led to a 43% reduction in the risk of progression or death (HR=0.57; [95% CI, 0.43, 0.76]; p<0.0001). The safety profile of BRUKINSA plus rituximab was consistent with the known safety profile of both medicines, with no new safety signals identified.

catalyst_text: Announced positive Phase 3 results in CLL
detailed_catalyst_text: Reported new Phase 3 SEQUOIA updates in treatment-naïve chronic lymphocytic leukemia, including an elderly (≥80) subgroup analysis showing durable efficacy and manageable safety. The 78‑month overall dataset showed progression-free survival of 71.8% versus 31.0% for bendamustine‑rituximab, while the ≥80 subgroup achieved 100% overall response with 72‑month PFS of 63.8%. These data provide long-term evidence supporting use in first-line CLL, including high-risk and very elderly patients.
catalyst_text_evidence: BeOne Medicines Ltd. (NASDAQ:ONC, HKEX: 06160, SSE: 688235)), a global oncology company, today announced the presentation of a large Phase 3 dataset in patients with chronic lymphocytic leukemia or small lymphocytic lymphoma (CLL/SLL) aged 80 and older, showing sustained benefit with BRUKINSA after nearly 6.5 years of follow-up, reinforcing its role as the foundational BTK inhibitor. In this analysis of SEQUOIA, 38 patients aged 80 or older at study entry received BRUKINSA. After a median follow-up of 78.8 months, BRUKINSA-treated patients continued to show durable benefit. Key highlights include: Overall response rate (ORR): 100%, with a complete response rate of 18.4%. 72-month progression-free survival (PFS): 63.8% (95% CI, 44.6–77.8). 72-month overall survival (OS): 75.9% (95% CI, 58.7–86.7). The subgroup analysis will be presented alongside the 78-month SEQUOIA dataset, the longest reported follow-up for a next-generation BTK inhibitor in first-line CLL, showing a 78-month PFS of 71.8% for BRUKINSA versus 31.0% for bendamustine-rituximab.

drug_indication: Chronic Lymphocytic Leukemia, Small Lymphocytic Lymphoma
catalyst_text: Reported positive long term Phase 3 CLL results
detailed_catalyst_text: Updated SEQUOIA Phase 3 results with a median follow-up of 84 months showed sustained progression-free survival benefit over bendamustine-rituximab in treatment-naïve CLL/SLL, with favorable TTNT and consistent safety. Multiple large real-world analyses also showed improved outcomes and lower atrial fibrillation rates versus other BTK inhibitors. These findings reinforce long-term disease control and support first-line use.
catalyst_text_evidence: After a median follow-up of 84.01 months (range, 0.0-101.5), BRUKINSA continued to show benefit over bendamustine-rituximab (BR) in patients with treatment-naive CLL/SLL, with progression-free survival (PFS) outcomes that are unprecedented among BTK inhibitors. 78-month PFS: 71.8% (95% CI, 65.3-77.3) for BRUKINSA vs. 31.0% (95% CI, 24.3-37.9) for BR. Time to next treatment (TTNT) favored BRUKINSA over BR (HR, 0.24; 95% CI, 0.16-0.35; P<.0001). In a real-world analysis of 10,523 Medicare patients… patients treated with BRUKINSA had a statistically significantly lower risk of death, advancing to next line, or discontinuing treatment, than those on ibrutinib or acalabrutinib. In a separate real-world analysis of Komodo database claims from 16,788 patients with treatment-naïve CLL, BRUKINSA had a longer TTNT… and overall survival (OS…). A retrospective analysis of 233,362 newly diagnosed CLL patients… the atrial fibrillation rate within 1 year was lowest for BRUKINSA at 11%….

catalyst_text: Received FDA approval for relapsed mantle cell lymphoma
detailed_catalyst_text: The BCL2 inhibitor received U.S. FDA approval for adult patients with relapsed or refractory mantle cell lymphoma after at least two prior systemic therapies, including a BTK inhibitor. This regulatory milestone enables availability for a defined R/R MCL population in the U.S. market.
catalyst_text_evidence: Additionally, BEQALZI (sonrotoclax), which was recently approved by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration, and its development in combination with BRUKINSA (ZS) highlight the potential for next-generation, time-limited treatment approaches in CLL. BEQALZI is approved by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) and China's National Medical Products Administration for the treatment of adult patients with relapsed or refractory (R/R) mantle cell lymphoma (MCL), after at least two lines of systemic therapy, including a BTK inhibitor.

drug_indication: Chronic Lymphocytic Leukemia, Small Lymphocytic Lymphoma
catalyst_text: Reported positive Phase 1b CLL combo results
detailed_catalyst_text: In a Phase 1/1b study in treatment‑naïve CLL/SLL, the all‑oral combination achieved 100% ORR with 59.5% complete responses and a best uMRD4 rate of 98.8%, including in high‑risk patients. Median time to uMRD4 was 4.5 months, and no progression events were observed at the RP2D, with safety consistent with prior experience. Results suggest potential for a time‑limited regimen with deep, durable responses.
catalyst_text_evidence: In the Phase 1/1b study in patients with treatment-naïve CLL/SLL (median follow-up of ~34 months), the all-oral combination of BRUKINSA and next-generation BCL2 inhibitor sonrotoclax (ZS) demonstrated unprecedented rates and kinetics of undetectable minimal residual disease (uMRD), including in patients with high-risk cytogenetics. Overall response rate (ORR): 100%, with complete responses in 59.5% of patients. Best uMRD4 rate 98.8%. Median time from combination start to uMRD4: 4.5 months. No disease progression events observed at the recommended Phase 2 dose of 320mg, including patients who electively discontinued therapy.

drug_indication: Relapsed or Refractory Mantle Cell Lymphoma
catalyst_text: Received FDA accelerated approval for the indication
detailed_catalyst_text: The FDA granted accelerated approval to sonrotoclax for adults with relapsed or refractory mantle cell lymphoma after at least two prior systemic therapies including a BTK inhibitor. The decision was supported by Phase 1/2 data showing a 52% overall response rate and 16% complete response rate. This provides a new targeted option for patients in the post‑BTK setting, addressing a significant unmet need.
catalyst_text_evidence: BeOne Medicines Ltd. ... announced that the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has granted accelerated approval to BEQALZI (bee-KAHL-zee; sonrotoclax) ... for the treatment of adult patients with relapsed or refractory (R/R) mantle cell lymphoma (MCL), after at least two lines of systemic therapy, including a Bruton's tyrosine kinase (BTK) inhibitor. Approval of BEQALZI marks the first new BCL2 inhibitor approved in a decade in the U.S. and the only BCL2 inhibitor approved in MCL, aiming to set a new standard of innovation.

catalyst_text: Received priority review and reported positive Phase 3
detailed_catalyst_text: FDA granted Priority Review to the sBLA for the combination with chemotherapy as a first-line treatment for unresectable locally advanced or metastatic HER2-positive gastroesophageal adenocarcinoma. The regimen also received Breakthrough Therapy Designation, and interim Phase 3 data from HERIZON-GEA-01 showed statistically significant overall survival and progression-free survival benefits, including a 26.4-month median OS with the triplet. This accelerates U.S. review and supports potential practice-changing impact in this setting.
catalyst_text_evidence: BeOne Medicines Ltd. (NASDAQ:ONC, HKEX: 06160, SSE: 688235)), a global oncology company, today announced that the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has granted Priority Review to a supplemental Biologics License Application (sBLA) for TEVIMBRA® (tislelizumab) in combination with ZIIHERA® (zanidatamab) and chemotherapy for the first-line treatment of unresectable locally advanced/metastatic HER2-positive (HER2) gastric, gastroesophageal junction, or esophageal adenocarcinoma. The FDA has also granted Breakthrough Therapy Designation to the regimen of ZIIHERA in combination with fluoropyrimidine- and platinum-containing chemotherapy, with and without TEVIMBRA, in this indication. The sBLA submission is based on the first interim analysis (IA1) of HERIZON-GEA-01, a global Phase 3 clinical trial designed to evaluate ZIIHERA plus chemotherapy, with and without TEVIMBRA, compared with the control arm of trastuzumab plus chemotherapy as first-line treatment for advanced/metastatic HER2+ GEA. Overall survival (OS): The arm in which TEVIMBRA was added to ZIIHERA and chemotherapy resulted in a statistically significant improvement in OS (median OS of 26.4 months) at IA1. The ZIIHERA plus chemotherapy arm achieved a median OS of 24.4 months and the control arm resulted in a median OS of 19.2 months. Progression-free survival (PFS): Both ZIIHERA-containing arms delivered a statistically significant and clinically meaningful improvement in median PFS of 12.4 months compared with 8.1 months in the control arm.

catalyst_text: Received FDA Fast Track designation for hepatocellular carcinoma
detailed_catalyst_text: FDA granted Fast Track Designation to the GPC3x4-1BB bispecific for adult hepatocellular carcinoma after progression on prior systemic therapy. A global Phase 1 trial is ongoing evaluating the therapy alone and in combination with a PD-1 inhibitor. Fast Track may expedite development and review in this high-need setting.
catalyst_text_evidence: the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has granted the Company Fast Track Designation for BGB-B2033, its GPC3x4-1BB bispecific antibody for the treatment of adult patients with hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) with disease progression on or after prior systemic treatment. BeOne is currently conducting a global, multi-center Phase 1 clinical trial (NCT06427941) to explore the safety and anti-tumor activity of BGB-B2033, both alone and in combination with PD-1 inhibitor TEVIMBRA (tislelizumab).
